newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
SUGAR - World market for August 29, 1996

White sugar futures in London ended lower in quiet trade. October rose $0.70 a tonne to $348.30. The market shrugged off news that Syria was open to buy 26,000 tonnes of white sugar and 26,000 tonnes of raws for October/November delivery to replace a cancelled tender.

In New York raw sugar futures ended little changed in quiet trade. October remained flat at 11.73 cents/lb while March gave up 1 point to close at 11.38 cents/lb. There were no fresh fundamental news to give the market direction.
FUNDAMENTALS -

INDIA - S.L. Jain, Secretary General of the Indian Sugar Mills Association, told Reuters that sugar production in 1996/97 (October/September) could fall to about 15 million tonnes, white value, down from 16.45 million tonnes expected for 1995/96. Jain said that he expects more sugar cane to be used in making jaggery and sulphur sugar in 1996/97, cutting production of mill white sugar.

Jain also said that cane production in 1996/97 could be 10 million tonnes lower than the 280 million tonnes expected for 1995/96 because of an anticipated reduction in cane production in the southern states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. Sugar consumption in 1996/97 is forecast to rise to 14 million tonnes up from the present 13 million tonnes. Exports so far have reached 798,000 tonnes out of the 1.0 million tonnes of exports allowed in 1995/96.

Traders said the remainder would be shipped by the middle of October. The government has authorized another 1 million tonnes for export in 1996/97 to help the industry getting rid of its sugar surplus.

AUSTRALIA - Sugar exports in May 1996 amounted to 67,839 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 217,873 tonnes. This brought total exports in 1995/96 (June/May) up to 4.17 million tonnes, down from 4.48 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Total sugar exports in 1993/94 amounted to 3.55 million tonnes. Major countries of destination in 1995/96 were Japan with 703,908 tonnes raws against 770,645 tonnes, Canada with 641,274 tonnes against 666,815 tonnes and South Korea with 604,589 tonnes, down from 734,409 tonnes.

New on the list of Australian raw sugar destinations in 1995/96 were Dubai (62,125 tonnes), Croatia (51,486 tonnes) the Baltic states Latvia and Lithuania with a total of 58,000 tonnes and the Philippines with 77,000 tonnes. Furthermore, Australia was able to boost its white sugar exports in 1995/96 to almost 235,000 tonnes, up from 146,000 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in 1995/96 were Indonesia with 59,435 tonnes against 19,461 tonnes, New Zealand with 33,180 tonnes against nil and Hong Kong with 30,399 tonnes compared to 10,111 tonnes.

GERMANY - Sugar production in July 1996 amounted to 742 tonnes which brought cumulative production in the first ten months of 1995/96 (October/July) up to 4.15 million tonnes, raw value, against 3.99 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total production in 1994/95 reached 3.99 million tonnes, down from 4.74 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Sugar consumption continues to develop favourably. Total offtake in July 1996 amounted to 287,785 tonnes, up from last year's 268,548 tonnes. This brought cumulative consumption in October/July 1995/96 up to 2.52 million tonnes, up from 2.45 million tonnes in 1994/95. Total consumption in 1994/95 amounted to 2.99 million tonnes against 2.94 million tonnes in 1993/94.
UNITED KINGDOM - The latest beet test of August 27 confirmed that the sugar crop is still struggling with below average beet weight and sugar content, although recent increases were satisfactory.

Root weight on 27 August reached 498 grams, up from 435 grams in 1995, but still below the 1991/95 average of 516 grams. Sugar content fell to 15.48 per cent against 18.54 per cent in 1995 and also below the average of 16.82 per cent.

This resulted in an average sugar weight per root of 77.1 grams, 8.8 grams more than in the previous test and 80.7 grams in 1995, after a rise of 6.2 grams. The average value stands at 86.8 grams after a rise of 9.5 grams. British Sugar emphasized that the crop is on course for an average result although additional rains are needed.
TENDERS -

Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) issued a new tender to buy 26,000 tonnes of white sugar and 26,000 tonnes of raws for October/November delivery. This tender replaces an earlier tender which was cancelled by GEZA because price offers did not meet its conditions.

Both the whites and the raws should be delivered between October 10 and November 10 in two equal cargoes of 13,000 tonnes each. Pakistan is considering buying another 200,000 tonnes of white sugar for delivery in September, official sources said.

Egypt will hold a buying tender for 25,000 tonnes of 150 ICUMSA quality white sugar on September 4. The sugar is for October/November delivery, but payment terms could limit participation to local companies, trade sources said.

The tender is in addition to one by the Egyptian state's Sugar and Integrated Industries Company due on September 17 for 25,000 tonnes of bulk raw sugar or packed white sugar at the buyer's option, trade sources said.
